title: Swarming reference stops contradicting the guard on tier transport
action: Three stale spots, per D1(a) and D1(c). (1) Lines 104-115, inside the `<!-- bee:only claude -->` block opening `**Spawn the tier-matched pinned type when its rendered agent exists**:`. Its sentence `\`ceiling\` has no rendered agent (it IS the session model) — spawn it as the runtime's default/general subagent type; the same default applies when the tier's slot is cli-shaped or otherwise has no rendered file.` is wrong for a cli- or herding-shaped slot: the guard denies such a dispatch outright (cli-tier-denied / herding-tier-denied), and at `generation` it denies `general-purpose` too (`generic-type-denied`). Keep the `ceiling` half — ceiling really is the runtime default type — and replace the 'same default applies' half with the real rule: a slot that resolves to no model is not a subagent at all, so resolve the transport with `.bee/bin/bee dispatch prepare --runtime claude --kind <cell|gather|reviewer|advisor> --json` and run the Bash payload it returns (per D1). (2) Line 300, the `| Subagent type |` table row, containing `\`ceiling\`, and any tier whose slot is cli-shaped or otherwise unrendered, use the runtime default (\`general-purpose\`)`. Same correction in table-cell form: ceiling uses the runtime default; a cli- or herding-shaped slot goes through `bee dispatch prepare`. Keep the row's existing final clause about the guard repairing a generic type for extraction and review and refusing at generation. (3) Lines 370-384, the `## Herding Execution — A Foreign Agent In A Pane` section. The sentences `Scope B (a \`{kind:"herding"}\` tier kind in \`models.*\`, picked automatically the way \`subagent\`/\`cli\` are today) is a separate, trigger-gated backlog item — it does not exist yet, and this reference never treats herding as something the tier judgment step (4, above) can select on its own.` are false: scope B shipped (herding-tier D1-D6, widened by herding-review-slots D1) and is what a host repo with `generation: {kind:"herding"}` runs. Rewrite that passage to say scope B exists and is selected automatically by `bee dispatch prepare` when the slot is herding-shaped, keeping scope A (the user naming one cell to run by hand) as the separate, still-accurate case. Leave the bee-ignorant-worker paragraph and the orchestrator loop that follow unchanged. Do not restructure sections or renumber the orchestrator steps.
verify: rg -n 'does not exist yet|use the runtime default \(`general-purpose`\)|the same default applies when the tier' skills/bee-swarming/references/swarming-reference.md; rg -n 'dispatch prepare' skills/bee-swarming/references/swarming-reference.md
